## SURFACE
Std Prusa/RepRap G-code. ASCII, LF endings, period-decimal, mm units, G90 absolute XY / M83 relative E. `M486` object-tracking ext (`Sn`=select obj id, `S-1`=deselect, `A"name"`=label). Quoted params on `M862.3`/`M862.6` look like data strings.

## CONTENT
Grep confirms only 2 `M486 A` labels total: `Embossed text` (line 26) and `Shape-Box` (line 29) — these tag *objects* in slicer's object list, not glyph content. Actual printed characters exist only as vector toolpath (thousands of X/Y moves per layer) — no literal string field anywhere encodes "what the text shows." Quoted strings elsewhere (`"MK4S"`, `"Input shaper"`) = printer-model/feature capability checks, unrelated to emboss text.

Mismatch: file *looks* like it should have a text field readable by grep, but real content only exists as geometry — must trace toolpath, not read label.

CONTENT VERDICT: MISMATCH

## MISREADINGS
1. **Hyp: `M486 AEmbossed text` = literal printed word.** Test: only 2 object labels exist, second one (`Shape-Box`) obviously a shape name not print text → labels are generic/default slicer object names, not verified glyph content. **Falsified as reliable source** — survives only as weak hint.
2. **Hyp: quoted strings `"MK4S"` / `"Input shaper"` hold text content.** Test: attached to `M862.3`/`M862.6`, standard Prusa firmware-compatibility check commands (printer model, feature gate) — unrelated command family. **Falsified.**
3. **Hyp: CRLF or decimal-comma locale corrupts number parsing.** Test: `xxd` shows pure `0a` (LF only), `grep -c ',[0-9]'` = 0. **Falsified**, no locale risk.
4. **Hyp: `M486 S0/S1/S-1` values are char/font codes.** Correct: `S`=object-index selector for exclude-object (id select / deselect), unrelated to character encoding. Risk: conflating index with ASCII code point.

Bottom line: answering "what text shows" needs geometric reconstruction of the toolpath (not done here per scope — audit only), not a text-field read.
